display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support is-finite in the block-level Triton emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support is-finite in the block-level Triton emitter.

Fusions containing `is-finite` previously fell back to the native emitters because `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` excluded `HloOpcode::kIsFinite` and Triton's `ConvertTritonToTritonGPU` pass does not legalize `math.isfinite`.

Add `HloOpcode::kIsFinite` for `f16`, `bf16`, `f32`, and `f64` in `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` and lower `math.isfinite` in `UnsupportedElementwiseToTritonPass` to `arith.cmpf one, math.absf(x), +inf`. Lowering in the Triton-specific pass preserves `math.isfinite` in the shared XTile emitter used by the CPU backend, avoids `third_party/triton` patches, and avoids libdevice call overhead and missing 16-bit libdevice helpers while matching the native MLIR emitter's IEEE-754 semantics (`±inf` and `±NaN` return `false`; finite values including `±0` and subnormals return `true`).

display_title: Finish the two heaps of the operand reuse comparison in parallel

head_commit.message:
Finish the two heaps of the operand reuse comparison in parallel

`HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse` simulates with and without the reuse of operand buffers through other positions and keeps the smaller heap. When it had to finish both heaps, it did that one after the other. Now the heap without the reuse is finished on a second thread.

`HeapAlgorithm::Finish()` only works on the data of its own heap, so the two calls do not share mutable state. The one exception was in `heap_simulator_test`: its fake heap counted the `Finish()` calls of both heaps in one `int`. That counter is atomic now.

display_title: PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

head_commit.message:
PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53709

📝 Summary of Changes

Fix copy insertion for stream-annotated computations on the parallel execution thread

🎯 Justification

computations annotated with _xla_stream_annotation (compute_on("gpu_stream:N")) run on the parallel execution thread. But RunPreSchedulingCopyInsertion still ran copy insertion only on main, so it skipped any while loop inside an annotated region. That loop never got the control edges or copies that copy insertion adds to keep in-place loop-carried updates safe.

As a result, the loop counter's in-place increment (i + 1) could be scheduled before the instructions that read i, and since buffer assignment gives i and i + 1 the same buffer, those readers saw the incremented value. A user's fori_loop with dynamic_slice/dynamic_update_slice on a second stream produced wrong results, with no error raised.

The fix runs the pre-scheduling copy-insertion pipeline on both the main and parallel threads.

The Triton scan emitter already handles reverse scans: it visits the tiles in reverse order and takes the carry from the first element of each tile. Padding a partial tile with zeros stays correct because only additive combiners are supported.

Remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`, so that `ScanRewriterTriton` also rewrites reverse scans.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Use zero-copy shared fake arguments in FunctionalHloRunner.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Use zero-copy shared fake arguments in FunctionalHloRunner.

`FunctionalHloRunner::CreateArgumentsOnDevice` previously materialized owned `Literal` copies for every parameter on every device (and built then decomposed owned wrapper tuples for single-tuple modules), holding gigabytes of transient host RAM alive during `CopyArgumentsToDevice` only to discard them immediately afterwards.

Refactor `CopyArgumentsToDevice` around a non-owning `absl::Span<const std::vector<const Literal*>>` view (with the `PerDeviceLiteralVecType` map overload as a thin wrapper) and switch `CreateArgumentsOnDevice` to `FakeArgumentsGenerator::MakeSharedArguments` and `MakeFlattenedSharedArguments`. Shared literal pointers stay alive until every `PjRtBuffer` ready future completes (including on error) and avoid redundant per-device generation when `use_shared_inputs` is active.

Measured in isolation on 8-device `-c opt` CPU runs of `hlo_runner_main` (`--hlo_argument_mode=use_random_inputs --random_seed=42`, medians over 5 interleaved A/B trials comparing this CL against its parent without zero-copy adoption in `FunctionalHloRunner`):
- 32-layer dense BF16 (64 params, 6 GiB): init+load 2.548s -> 0.770s (3.31x speedup, -1.78s), peak RSS 12.63 GiB -> 6.62 GiB (1.91x lower, -6.01 GiB)
- 64-leaf single-tuple BF16 (4 GiB): init+load 1.382s -> 0.399s (3.47x speedup, -0.98s), peak RSS 8.37 GiB -> 4.37 GiB (1.92x lower, -4.00 GiB)
- 8-layer MoE-like (32 bulk + 16 uncached small routers, 4 GiB): init+load 1.556s -> 0.543s (2.86x speedup, -1.01s), peak RSS 8.55 GiB -> 4.55 GiB (1.88x lower, -4.01 GiB)
- 1,000-param / 25k-op mixed (32 bulk + 968 small, 4 GiB): init+load 2.075s -> 1.085s (1.91x speedup, -0.99s), peak RSS 8.84 GiB -> 4.83 GiB (1.83x lower, -4.01 GiB)

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1029826349

display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

The heap simulator only lets an instruction reuse the buffer of an operand value if it consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. Reusing it also through instructions that forward the value (e.g. `get-tuple-element`, `bitcast`, `opt-barrier`, `call`) lowers the peak memory, but can add more fragmentation than it saves.

`BufferAssigner` now calls the new `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`. It simulates with and without this kind of reuse and keeps it only if the heap is smaller. Algorithms with a slow `Finish()` drop it without comparing if it does not lower the peak memory. The comparison is per heap simulation, so the fallback chain can stop at an earlier algorithm than before. Other callers of `HeapSimulator::Run` do not change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022733837

native reduction emitters by enabling `shift-left`, `shift-right-logical`, and
`shift-right-arithmetic` across all Triton-supported integral types (`S8`,
`S16`, `S32`, `S64`, `U8`, `U16`, `U32`, `U64`). Previously, fusions containing
shift operations (such as reductions over shifted inputs) were rejected during
Triton support checking as unsupported elementwise operations.

### Summary of Changes
- **Support check** (`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/support.cc`): Enable
  `kShiftLeft`, `kShiftRightArithmetic`, and `kShiftRightLogical` in
  `TritonSupportedBinaryElementwiseOps` for integral types (excluding `S4`/`U4`
  and `PRED`).
- **XTile emission & verification** (`xla/codegen/xtile/codegen/emitter_helpers.cc`,
  `xla/codegen/xtile/ir/transforms/verify_legal_xtile_ops.cc`): Emit and allow
  `stablehlo.shift_left`, `stablehlo.shift_right_logical`, and
  `stablehlo.shift_right_arithmetic`.
- **StableHLO-to-Arith lowering** (`xla/codegen/xtile/ir/transforms/lower_stablehlo_to_arith.cc`):
  Lower all three shift ops to `arith.shli` / `arith.shrui` / `arith.shrsi`
  (converting unsigned operands to signless as needed) while preserving XLA's
  defined saturation semantics for out-of-bounds shift amounts
  (`arith.cmpi ult, rhs, bitwidth`): saturate to `0` for `shift-left` and
  `shift-right-logical`, and to `arith.shrsi(lhs, bitwidth - 1)` for
  `shift-right-arithmetic`. Performing this lowering directly in
  `StablehloLowerToArithPass` keeps the IR immediately sound before
  canonicalization and lets constant shift amounts fold away cleanly.
- **Tests**: Add FileCheck lowering tests in
  `xla/codegen/xtile/ir/transforms/tests/lower_stablehlo_to_arith.mlir` and
  GPU execution tests covering out-of-bounds/negative shift amounts and
  shift+reduction fusions in
  `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests/fusion_emitter_device_test.cc`.

display_title: Add shared-literal fake argument APIs to FakeArgumentsGenerator.

head_commit.message:
Add shared-literal fake argument APIs to FakeArgumentsGenerator.

`FakeArgumentCache` already stores cached tensors as `std::shared_ptr<const Literal>`, yet `MakeFakeArguments` always calls `CloneArrayLiteralParallel` on every cache hit and miss. In multi-device runners, this allocates and copies gigabytes of transient host RAM (and builds an owned wrapper tuple before flattening single-tuple modules) even when callers only read the literals during host-to-device transfer.

Add `FakeArgumentsGenerator::MakeSharedArguments` and `FakeArgumentsGenerator::MakeFlattenedSharedArguments` returning `std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const Literal>>`. Default-memory-space cached array literals are returned directly from the cache without cloning; non-default memory spaces (such as `Layout::kHostMemorySpace` / `S(5)`) and non-flattened tuples fall back to cloning into owned literals. Also group literal generation options into a local struct and guard scalar identity-constant synthesis so flattened tuples containing a reduction-init scalar do not corrupt non-scalar or nested-tuple elements.

Measured in isolation via `-c opt` `test_utils_test_cpu` microbenchmarks (`--benchmark_filter=BM_Make.*`, medians over 5 interleaved A/B trials comparing `MakeArguments` vs. the new shared APIs with `cache_arguments = true`):
- Flat 64x `bf16[2048,4096]` (1 GiB/call, cold cache: 2 generated variants + 62 hits): 236.0ms -> 27.8ms (8.5x speedup), peak RSS 1,463 MiB -> 450 MiB (3.25x lower, -1,013 MiB)
- Flat 64x `bf16[2048,4096]` (1 GiB/call, warm cache: 64 hits): 86.6ms -> 71.7us (1,208x speedup), peak RSS 1,493 MiB -> 450 MiB (3.32x lower, -1,042 MiB)
- Single-tuple 64x `bf16[1024,4096]` (512 MiB/call, cold cache, `MakeArguments + DecomposeTuple()` vs. `MakeFlattenedSharedArguments`): 48.0ms -> 16.0ms (3.0x speedup), peak RSS 967 MiB -> 427 MiB (2.26x lower, -540 MiB)
- Single-tuple 64x `bf16[1024,4096]` (512 MiB/call, warm cache): 32.2ms -> 70.7us (455x speedup), peak RSS 966 MiB -> 426 MiB (2.27x lower, -540 MiB)

name: CI
display_title: Support kShuffle in SPMD partitioning and cross-device collective lowering

head_commit.message:
Support kShuffle in SPMD partitioning and cross-device collective lowering

Extend the SPMD partitioner (`SpmdPartitioningVisitor`) to natively partition
first-class `HloOpcode::kShuffle` (`HloShuffleInstruction`) operations across
sharded tensor dimensions, lowering sharded rotations into cross-device
collective right-rotate custom calls (`RotateRight`).

Only shuffles in `rotate` mode can be turned into a right-rotate collective, so
the pattern matching below is gated on the mode; other modes fall through to the existing handling.

Specifically, this commit introduces:
* **Sharding Propagation for kShuffle (`sharidng_propagation.cc`)**:
  - Support spatial partitioning for kShuffle if SPMD.
* **Pattern Matching & Utilities (`spmd_partitioner_util.h/cc`)**:
  - Generalize `FindRotateRightPattern` to return
    `std::optional<RotateRightPatternMatch>` containing
    `{dim, amount, rotate_dim_idx}`, enabling it to match both sharded
    rotate-mode `HloShuffleInstruction` operations and the traditional
    `kConcatenate` of slices pattern.
  - Add `PopRotateDimension` helper to pop a handled `(dimension, shift)` pair
    in-place from a multi-dimensional rotate-mode `HloShuffleInstruction`. When
    all shuffled dimensions are popped, it removes the instruction and replaces
    uses with `operand(0)`.
* **SPMD Partitioner (`spmd_partitioner.cc`)**:
  - Update `PartitionComputation` to loop over `FindRotateRightPattern(hlo)`
    matches, emitting `CreateCustomCallSPMDInternal_RotateRight` collective
    operations along sharded dimensions.
  - Use `PopRotateDimension` when matching `kShuffle` (`rotate_dim_idx >= 0`)
    so multi-dimensional rotations can peel off sharded dimensions one by one
    while preserving any remaining unpartitioned dimensions.
* **Testing**: Add unit tests in `SpmdPartitioningTest` and
  `SPMDPartitionerUtilTest` covering single- and multi-dimensional sharded
  `kShuffle` partitioning and pattern matching. Add test in
  `ShardingPropagationTest` to ensure sharding gets propagated through shuffle.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow reverse scans in Triton.

The Triton scan emitter already handles reverse scans: it visits the tiles in reverse order and takes the carry from the first element of each tile. Padding a partial tile with zeros stays correct because only additive combiners are supported.

Remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`, so that `ScanRewriterTriton` also rewrites reverse scans.

display_title: PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

head_commit.message:
PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53709

📝 Summary of Changes

Fix copy insertion for stream-annotated computations on the parallel execution thread

🎯 Justification

computations annotated with _xla_stream_annotation (compute_on("gpu_stream:N")) run on the parallel execution thread. But RunPreSchedulingCopyInsertion still ran copy insertion only on main, so it skipped any while loop inside an annotated region. That loop never got the control edges or copies that copy insertion adds to keep in-place loop-carried updates safe.

As a result, the loop counter's in-place increment (i + 1) could be scheduled before the instructions that read i, and since buffer assignment gives i and i + 1 the same buffer, those readers saw the incremented value. A user's fori_loop with dynamic_slice/dynamic_update_slice on a second stream produced wrong results, with no error raised.

The fix runs the pre-scheduling copy-insertion pipeline on both the main and parallel threads.

head_commit.message:
Add shuffle expander pass for kShuffle.

Extend the HLO optimization pipeline with an expander for
`HloOpcode::kShuffle`, allowing compiler pipelines to expand them into known ops when target backends do not provide native rotate lowering.

Specifically, this commit introduces:
* **ShuffleExpander (`shuffle_expander.h/cc`)**: Add an `OpExpanderPass` that decomposes `kShuffle::kRotate` instructions into a sequence of `kSlice` and `kConcatenate` operations (`concat(slice(shift:), slice(0:shift))`) along each rotated dimension for backends without native rotation support.
* **Testing**: Add comprehensive unit tests in `ShuffleExpanderTest`.

display_title: PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

head_commit.message:
PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49692

Previously, when a task failed during GPU clique initialization, `AbortCliques` only checked `state.cliques`. However, the clique isn't added there until initialization finishes, so the cancellation token was still in `pending_cliques`. I changed this so that `AbortCliques` also cancels the tokens in `pending_cliques`.

I tested this before and after the change. Before the fix, the cancellation token wasn't cancelled during initialization. After the fix, it was cancelled, allowing non-blocking initialization to stop.

This PR doesn't make blocking initialization or blocking `ncclCommSplit` check the cancellation token. For non-blocking init, the communicator handle is available before initialization finishes, so `ncclCommAbort` can clean it up if polling fails. However, for non-blocking split, `newcomm` remains `NCCL_COMM_NULL` until the split finishes, so the same cleanup doesn't work.

So for split, this PR only fixes cancellation of the pending token, not the actual NCCL split operation. I also added a CPU-only test to verify that the pending split token gets cancelled when a task fails, but it doesn't test whether the actual NCCL split stops.

display_title: Compare PrecisionConfig semantically in HloInstruction::IdenticalSlowPath

head_commit.message:
Compare PrecisionConfig semantically in HloInstruction::IdenticalSlowPath

`IdenticalSlowPath` (and `HashAdditionalAttributes` on dots) currently compares and hashes `precision_config()` by raw proto serialization, treating empty `operand_precision` and trailing `DEFAULT` entries (as produced by `CreateFromProto`) as unequal even though `PrintPrecisionConfig` omits both.

Compare and hash `PrecisionConfig` semantically via `PrecisionConfigsIdentical` and `HashPrecisionConfig`, ignoring trailing `DEFAULT` `operand_precision` entries so `Identical`, `AbslHashValue`, and HLO printing agree.

display_title: Avoid double-pushing tombstones in HloComputation constructor

head_commit.message:
Avoid double-pushing tombstones in HloComputation constructor

When `HloComputation` is constructed with `preserve_instruction_ids=true` (such as from `HloComputation::CreateFromProto` on a computation containing deleted-instruction local ID gaps), it pre-allocates `instructions_.resize(max_instruction_local_id + 1)`, which already populates every gap index with an empty `HloInstructionInfo`. However, the subsequent loop still calls `instructions_.push_back(HloInstructionInfo())` for every `nullptr` entry in `*instructions`. This appends `num_gaps` duplicate trailing tombstones to `instructions_` and inflates `next_instruction_unique_id_` by `num_gaps`, shifting the `local_id` and `unique_id` of every instruction subsequently added to the computation. Additionally, if a `nullptr` entry is encountered with `preserve_instruction_ids=false`, pushing without incrementing `next_instruction_unique_id_` violates the `next_instruction_unique_id_ == instructions_.size()` invariant on the next instruction.

Initialize `next_instruction_unique_id_` to `instructions_.size()` after pre-allocating for `preserve_instruction_ids=true`, skip `push_back` on `nullptr` entries when slots were already pre-allocated, and increment `next_instruction_unique_id_` if a `nullptr` gap is appended when `preserve_instruction_ids=false`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1030576451

display_title: [XLA] Reuse HloDataflowAnalysis once per module via FakeArgumentsGenerator.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reuse HloDataflowAnalysis once per module via FakeArgumentsGenerator.

`FunctionalHloRunner::CreateArgumentsOnDevice` previously called `MakeFakeArguments` once per addressable device, re-running single-threaded `HloDataflowAnalysis::Run(*module)` on every device iteration.

Add a move-only `FakeArgumentsGenerator` class that computes and owns `HloDataflowAnalysis` once for a single `HloModule` and exposes `MakeArguments(options)` for repeated generation across devices. This hides the dataflow-analysis dependency from callers and prevents module- or flag-mismatch bugs by construction. `FunctionalHloRunner::CreateArgumentsOnDevice` now constructs one generator per module (after validating `flatten_arguments`) and reuses it across all addressable devices.

Measured on 8-device `-c opt` CPU runs of `hlo_runner_main` (`--hlo_argument_mode=use_random_inputs --random_seed=42`, medians over 5 interleaved A/B trials):
- 500 params, 12k ops (`bf16[16,16]`): argument init+load 0.168s -> 0.037s (4.52x speedup, -131ms)
- 1,500 params, 33k ops (`bf16[16,16]`): argument init+load 0.483s -> 0.136s (3.56x speedup, -348ms)
- 1,000 params, 25k ops (32 bulk sharded weights + 968 small params, 4 GiB): argument init+load 2.760s -> 2.313s (1.19x speedup, -447ms)

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1025437694

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Accept scalar constant operands in softmax diamonds

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Accept scalar constant operands in softmax diamonds

SoftmaxRewriterTriton accepts a binary elementwise op inside a normalization
diamond if exactly one operand is a broadcast of a scalar constant or of a
parameter. When the reduction result is a scalar, the constant is used
directly, without a broadcast, and the diamond was rejected. An example is
x / maximum(sum(x), epsilon) on a rank-1 x.

Treat a scalar constant operand like a splat.

head_commit.message:
PR #53920: [ROCm] Fix TSAN data race in RecoverExp2Pattern static logs2_ init

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53920

📝 Summary of Changes
Guard the one-time lazy initialization of the class-static `RecoverExp2Pattern::logs2_` table in `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/recover_exp2.cc` with an `absl::once_flag` + `absl::call_once`.

🎯 Justification
`RecoverExp2Pass::runOnOperation` builds a new `RecoverExp2Pattern` on every run, and the pattern's constructor lazily fills the shared static `logs2_` array. Kernel compilation runs this pass on several threads at once, so several threads can read `logs2_` (`recover_exp2.cc:124`) while another thread writes it (`prefillLogs2From`, `recover_exp2.cc:104`). The values written are identical, but this is still a C++ data race. It fails 7 GPU test targets in the ROCm nightly TSAN job (`execute-xla-ut-sanitizers (tsan)`, "Test XLA [tsan] [single_gpu]"), including `matrix_ops_simple_test`, `prng_test` and `cholesky_test`. `absl::call_once` computes the table exactly once and safely publishes it to every thread that constructs the pattern. After the first call, the fast path is a single atomic load.

This addresses only this one race. Other TSAN reports on the same nightly job are separate issues: FissionBackend's shared `HloPassPipeline`, PJRT client lifetime and compute-stream events, and LLVM `TargetRegistry` init.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

To replace the runtime CUB FFI custom-call handlers with AOT-embeddable thunks, the compiler needs to turn a `CubSortExecutionPlan` and the embedded CUBIN kernel specs into an executable `ThunkSequence`.

So this change adds `cub_sort_thunk_emitter` and `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_registration` as `cuda-only` targets using the native custom-call thunk-folding infrastructure (`NativeCustomCallHandlerRegistry`), avoiding any `if_cuda_is_configured` branching or non-CUDA stubs. The emitter computes Onesweep histogram occupancy statically from `DeviceDescription` and CUBIN ELF attributes via `cuda_occupancy.h`, packs kernel arguments via `KernelArgsPackingSpec`, and emits a flat `ThunkSequence` of `CustomKernelThunk`s with strict pure-Read/pure-Write `BufferUse` slices for `CommandBufferThunk` capture and update.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add cluster barrier scope and DSMEM ops to xla_gpu dialect

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add cluster barrier scope and DSMEM ops to xla_gpu dialect

XLA:GPU supports launching kernels with CTA cluster dimensions on Hopper+ GPUs,
but `xla_gpu` MLIR emitters have no IR primitives to synchronize across CTAs in
a cluster or access peer CTAs' shared memory (DSMEM). This prepares the dialect
and lowering pipeline for upcoming clustered MLIR emitters (e.g. multi-CTA
bitonic sort) that exchange data across CTAs without global-memory round-trips.

- Add an optional `gpu::BarrierScope` attribute (default `Workgroup`) to
  `xla_gpu.sync_threads`, preserve it in `FlattenTensorsPass`, and forward it
  to `gpu.barrier` in GPU `LowerTensorsPass`.
- Add `xla_gpu.dsmem_extract` and `xla_gpu.dsmem_insert` ops taking an explicit
  cluster CTA rank and CTA-local index on 1D shared-memory tensors.
- Lower DSMEM ops via `nvvm.mapa` in GPU `LowerTensorsPass` (reusing a shared
  `EmitTensorElementStore` helper in `lower_tensors_common`), rejecting DSMEM
  ops and cluster barriers on unsupported targets and non-shared-memory DSMEM
  operands.

display_title: [ROCm] Stage no per-arch ROCm device files in CPU-only test jobs

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Stage no per-arch ROCm device files in CPU-only test jobs

Tests in the ROCm CPU job run no GPU code but staged per-arch device files
(MIOpen CK libraries and databases, rocBLAS and hipBLASLt kernels, kpack
files), about 1 GB per test for gfx950, which might push test inputs
over the RBE 4 GB input limit.

--@local_config_rocm//rocm:stage_device_files=false drops those files from
run-time data; the ROCm libraries are still staged and device code is still
compiled for TF_ROCM_AMDGPU_TARGETS. It is a build flag rather than a
repo_env so that switching it between CI steps does not re-run
@local_config_rocm. ci_rocm_cpu sets it.

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] remove obsolete msan annotations / flags

The annotations are now obsolete; XLA:CPU now has full msan support.
Without the annotation in SortThunk, msan now reports comparisons of
uninitialized data in jit-compiled sort comparators, as it does for C++
comparators.

The flag passed to XLA via --xla_backend_extra_options, which was
introduced by https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611, is also
removed now since it has been superseded by tfcompile's --sanitize_memory.

The annotation in tf2xla's MallocContiguousBuffers stays: not all
AOT-compiled code that runs in msan builds is instrumented yet.

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] tfcompile: default to memory-optimized schedule

Using the concurrency-optimized schedule in tfcompile wastes memory,
because tfcompile's default runtime cannot take advantage of
concurrency. Default to using the memory-optimized schedule to save
memory. The nanort runtime (--use_xla_nanort_runtime) can use a thread
pool; its users can still opt into the concurrency-optimized schedule
via tf_library's xla_flags.

display_title: [xla:cpu] add a runtime bridge to msan's thread-local variables

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] add a runtime bridge to msan's thread-local variables

msan-instrumented code passes shadow memory through msan's thread-local
variables (e.g. __msan_param_tls), which code compiled by XLA:CPU cannot
access directly. Following
https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT, add
__xla_cpu_runtime_emutls_get_address, which returns the address of the
calling thread's msan TLS variable for a given selector, and register it
as a builtin symbol. Code compiled with emulated TLS can then reach
msan's TLS through it.

Nothing calls the bridge yet.

pass them from xla_aot_compile_cpu when the target is built with

name: CI
display_title: [re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

head_commit.message:
[re-land #2][xla:cpu] add full msan support

Msan support is currently incomplete.  For example, we don't add
the appropriate msan pass to LLVM's pipeline; instead, we manually
call __msan_unpoison here and there. In AOT (tfcompile) the situation
is even worse, since we only add these annotations to some of the
emitted code.

This change adds complete support for msan (and msan-track-origins)
to XLA:CPU in both JIT and AOT modes. In particular:

- Adds a single boolean config flag to determine whether msan should
  be enabled in compiled code. This is then wired up through the
  compiler, removing several #ifdef MEMORY_SANITIZER (or equivalent)
  checks that we had scattered around the code base. (OK, this is
  two knobs because we also support track-origins.)
- Adds the msan pass to LLVM as documented in
    https://github.com/google/sanitizers/wiki/MemorySanitizerJIT
  This requires a small TLS emulation library, which (1) in JIT
  gives access to host symbols from JIT'ed code, and (2) in AOT
  (tfcompile) must be linked in the final binary so that the
  compiled code can reliably access msan symbols.

A couple of upstream LLVM bugs (fixes are under review) require
some workarounds:
- Disable SVE on AArch64 when msan is enabled, since LLVM's
  MemorySanitizer can't handle scalable vectors yet.
- Disable AVX2 on x86 hosts without AVX512BW+VLX when msan is
  enabled, since LLVM's X86 backend can't select bf16 broadcasts
  there yet.

What's missing from this CL:
1. Removal of now obsolete annotations
2. Setting of the appropriate flags in tfcompile to enable the
  new path in AOT.

These two missing changes will land once users have had time to recompile
their compilers (in case they embed tfcompile into them), about
1-2 weeks.

Note: the msan support implemented in this CL supersedes
https://github.com/openxla/xla/commit/70f2607611. That means the
xla_backend_extra option added there for msan on AOT will be removed when
landing the two missing pieces from this CL.

Reverts 3b900dd1a9e09783eec4a910220dfad75f068f3c

display_title: [xla:cpu] mark kernel and comparator return values noundef

head_commit.message:
[xla:cpu] mark kernel and comparator return values noundef

Clang marks scalar and pointer return values of C++ functions noundef,
including at the host's calls to XLA:CPU kernels and sort comparators.
Mark them noundef on the callee side too.

This is needed for msan: with eager checks, which Clang enables by
default (-fsanitize-memory-param-retval), the caller ignores the shadow
of noundef return values. Without noundef on the callee side,
msan-instrumented XLA:CPU code would pass that shadow anyway, and
uninitialized comparator results would go unreported. With noundef, the
callee checks its return value instead.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1030194016

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add cluster barrier scope and DSMEM ops to xla_gpu dialect

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add cluster barrier scope and DSMEM ops to xla_gpu dialect

XLA:GPU supports launching kernels with CTA cluster dimensions on Hopper+ GPUs,
but `xla_gpu` MLIR emitters have no IR primitives to synchronize across CTAs in
a cluster or access peer CTAs' shared memory (DSMEM). This prepares the dialect
and lowering pipeline for upcoming clustered MLIR emitters (e.g. multi-CTA
bitonic sort) that exchange data across CTAs without global-memory round-trips.

- Add an optional `gpu::BarrierScope` attribute (default `Workgroup`) to
  `xla_gpu.sync_threads`, preserve it in `FlattenTensorsPass`, and forward it
  to `gpu.barrier` in GPU `LowerTensorsPass`.
- Add `xla_gpu.dsmem_extract` and `xla_gpu.dsmem_insert` ops taking an explicit
  cluster CTA rank and CTA-local index on 1D shared-memory tensors.
- Lower DSMEM ops via `nvvm.mapa` in GPU `LowerTensorsPass` (reusing a shared
  `EmitTensorElementStore` helper in `lower_tensors_common`), rejecting DSMEM
  ops and cluster barriers on unsupported targets and non-shared-memory DSMEM
  operands.

display_title: PR #53920: [ROCm] Fix TSAN data race in RecoverExp2Pattern static logs2_ init

head_commit.message:
PR #53920: [ROCm] Fix TSAN data race in RecoverExp2Pattern static logs2_ init

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53920

📝 Summary of Changes
Guard the one-time lazy initialization of the class-static `RecoverExp2Pattern::logs2_` table in `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/recover_exp2.cc` with an `absl::once_flag` + `absl::call_once`.

🎯 Justification
`RecoverExp2Pass::runOnOperation` builds a new `RecoverExp2Pattern` on every run, and the pattern's constructor lazily fills the shared static `logs2_` array. Kernel compilation runs this pass on several threads at once, so several threads can read `logs2_` (`recover_exp2.cc:124`) while another thread writes it (`prefillLogs2From`, `recover_exp2.cc:104`). The values written are identical, but this is still a C++ data race. It fails 7 GPU test targets in the ROCm nightly TSAN job (`execute-xla-ut-sanitizers (tsan)`, "Test XLA [tsan] [single_gpu]"), including `matrix_ops_simple_test`, `prng_test` and `cholesky_test`. `absl::call_once` computes the table exactly once and safely publishes it to every thread that constructs the pattern. After the first call, the fast path is a single atomic load.

This addresses only this one race. Other TSAN reports on the same nightly job are separate issues: FissionBackend's shared `HloPassPipeline`, PJRT client lifetime and compute-stream events, and LLVM `TargetRegistry` init.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

display_title: PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

head_commit.message:
PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46400

#ai-generated

**Fixes:** #37181

**Summary of Changes**
Changed `-nvptx-prec-divf32` from `1` (`div.full`, 2 ULP error) to `2` (`div.rnd`, IEEE-754 compliant) in the NVPTX backend. LLVM already defaults to `2`; XLA was overriding it.

**Justification**
GPU float32 division produces non-IEEE-754 results: `a/a` evaluates to `0.99999994` instead of `1.0` for many f32 values. This violates user expectations and breaks numerical invariants. The issue was confirmed on RTX 3090 (JAX 0.6.0) in #37181.

**Kind of Contribution**
Bug Fix

**Benchmark**
N/A — this is a correctness fix, not a performance change. The original `=1` override was added for "float-division heavy benchmarks" but `div.full` trades correctness for speed; `div.rnd` is LLVM's default and is IEEE-754 compliant with >1 ULP accuracy.

**Unit Tests**
New regression test: `xla/tests/ieee_f32_division_test.cc` (registered as `//xla/tests:ieee_f32_division_test`, runs on cpu+gpu) asserts the IEEE-754 identity properties `x / x == 1.0` and `x / 1.0 == x` that the `div.full` override broke, across values including `FLT_MAX`, `FLT_MIN`, `1e10`, `1e-10`. It uses parameters and disabled fast math so the division is actually executed by the backend rather than folded or simplified away. Existing GPU backend tests continue to pass: `nvptx_backend_test`, `load_ir_module_test`, `utils_test`, `nvptx_utils_test`.

**Execution Tests**
A standalone reproducer script is available at `repro_xla_37181.py` that verifies IEEE-754 division compliance across 5 categories (identity, inverse, overflow, underflow, NaN).

[XLA:GPU] Add regression test for IEEE-754 f32 division

The NVPTX backend was overriding LLVM's IEEE-754 compliant f32 division
(div.rn) with div.full, which has up to 2 ULP of error and made e.g.

xla/tests/ieee_f32_division_test.cc asserting the IEEE-754 identity
properties x / x == 1.0 and x / 1.0 == x that the div.full override
breaks. Parameters and disabled fast math are used so the division is
actually executed by the backend rather than folded or simplified.

Merging this change closes #46400

display_title: [XLA:Python] Add backend_config dedup to as_serialized_hlo_module_proto

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Python] Add backend_config dedup to as_serialized_hlo_module_proto

Problem: `HloModule.as_serialized_hlo_module_proto()` always calls
`HloModule::ToProto()` with default `HloProtoOptions`, inlining every
instruction's `backend_config`. On large unrolled modules with repeated custom
calls, the serialized `HloModuleProto` can exceed the 2 GiB protobuf limit and
fail serialization.

Solution: Expose optional `deduplicate_backend_config` (default `False`) and
`min_backend_config_size` (default `0`) arguments on
`HloModule.as_serialized_hlo_module_proto()` in `xla/python/hlo.cc` and
`xla/python/_hlo.pyi`, rejecting negative `min_backend_config_size` with
`InvalidArgument`. Default behavior is unchanged.

display_title: PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

head_commit.message:
PR #49692: [xla:gpu] Cancel in-progress GPU clique init on task failure

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49692

Previously, when a task failed during GPU clique initialization, `AbortCliques` only checked `state.cliques`. However, the clique isn't added there until initialization finishes, so the cancellation token was still in `pending_cliques`. I changed this so that `AbortCliques` also cancels the tokens in `pending_cliques`.

I tested this before and after the change. Before the fix, the cancellation token wasn't cancelled during initialization. After the fix, it was cancelled, allowing non-blocking initialization to stop.

This PR doesn't make blocking initialization or blocking `ncclCommSplit` check the cancellation token. For non-blocking init, the communicator handle is available before initialization finishes, so `ncclCommAbort` can clean it up if polling fails. However, for non-blocking split, `newcomm` remains `NCCL_COMM_NULL` until the split finishes, so the same cleanup doesn't work.

So for split, this PR only fixes cancellation of the pending token, not the actual NCCL split operation. I also added a CPU-only test to verify that the pending split token gets cancelled when a task fails, but it doesn't test whether the actual NCCL split stops.

display_title: [xla:gpu] Expose registered device descriptions on `_gpu_spec.GpuTargetConfig`

head_commit.message:
[xla:gpu] Expose registered device descriptions on `_gpu_spec.GpuTargetConfig`

A GPU model can report more than one device description at runtime, e.g. an H200 shows up as either "NVIDIA H200 141GB HBM3e" or "NVIDIA H200". `device_description_str` holds only one of them, so Python callers that resolve a device kind to a spec missed the others. `device_descriptions` lists every description registered for the model in `GetSupportedGpuPlatformConfigs`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB segmented radix sort kernels

Batched sorts whose segment size exceeds a single thread-block tile need a multi-pass segmented radix sort kernel. XLA's existing `DeviceSegmentedRadixSort` wrapper copies per-segment offset arrays H2D on every call and ties the runtime to CUB.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points (`CubUniformSegmentedRadixSort{Keys,Pairs}Kernel`) with both primary and alternate radix bit-width policies across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Because XLA batched sorts have uniform segment sizes, each thread block computes its segment base offset directly from `blockIdx.x * segment_size`, avoiding the per-call H2D offset buffer copy while keeping each pass pure-Read/pure-Write for command buffers.

head_commit.message:
Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

Updates `.github/workflows/bazel_dependency_violations.yml` to run 3 parallel
jobs—one per build configuration:
- `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: consolidates the 3 CPU checks (`gpu`,
  `cuda-only`, `rocm-only`) into separate steps sharing one warm Bazel server,
  saving ~2 cold runner invocations per PR while preserving per-tag step
  reporting and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` output.
- `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build` (`--config=cuda_clang`)
- `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build` (`--config=rocm_clang_hermetic`)

Extracts the per-tag `bazel cquery` check into
`build_tools/dependencies/check_dependency_violations.sh`, triggers `cquery`
when the workflow or dependency-check scripts themselves change, and bumps the
job timeout from 10 to 15 minutes to accommodate the hermetic ROCm download.

Observed GitHub Actions durations (when build/config files change):
- Before (3 separate CPU jobs): ~3m 20s – 5m 30s each (~11m 50s – 12m 30s total
  runner time; ~5m wall-clock).
- After (3 parallel jobs across CPU, CUDA, and ROCm):
  - `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: ~3m 30s – 3m 45s (the 2nd and 3rd `cquery`
    steps take only ~1–4s on the warm Bazel server, saving ~8.5 runner-min).
  - `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build`: ~4m 10s – 6m 05s.
  - `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build`: ~6m 40s – 7m 10s (~8m headroom under
    the 15-minute timeout).
  - Total: ~14m 30s – 16m 45s runner time (~7m wall-clock) for all 3 configs.

Temporarily keeps lightweight pass-through stub jobs (~5s each on
`ubuntu-latest`) for the legacy `no-cuda-only-targets-in-cpu-build` and
`no-rocm-only-targets-in-cpu-build` check names during the transition; a
follow-up change removes them once CI configs stop waiting on those names.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB Onesweep radix sort kernels

Unbatched sorts larger than a single thread-block tile need a multi-block GPU sort algorithm to avoid falling back to slower sorting paths or linking CUB's runtime host dispatcher.

So this change adds XLA-owned embeddable CUDA device entry points for CUB's multi-portion Onesweep radix sort across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types: the value-independent histogram kernel (compiled once per key type in the keys-only shards and reused by pair shards), an out-of-place exclusive-sum kernel (`cub_sort_kernels_exclusive_sum.cu.cc`) that also zeroes per-(portion, pass) dynamic tile counters, and the Onesweep scatter kernels. `GetCubSortOnesweepKernelSpecs` extracts the single-architecture CUBINs together with statically parsed histogram register/shared-memory attributes for compile-time occupancy planning.

display_title: PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

head_commit.message:
PR #53709: [XLA:GPU] Fix copy insertion to add the correct parallel threads to copies in loops

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53709

📝 Summary of Changes

Fix copy insertion for stream-annotated computations on the parallel execution thread

🎯 Justification

computations annotated with _xla_stream_annotation (compute_on("gpu_stream:N")) run on the parallel execution thread. But RunPreSchedulingCopyInsertion still ran copy insertion only on main, so it skipped any while loop inside an annotated region. That loop never got the control edges or copies that copy insertion adds to keep in-place loop-carried updates safe.

As a result, the loop counter's in-place increment (i + 1) could be scheduled before the instructions that read i, and since buffer assignment gives i and i + 1 the same buffer, those readers saw the incremented value. A user's fori_loop with dynamic_slice/dynamic_update_slice on a second stream produced wrong results, with no error raised.

The fix runs the pre-scheduling copy-insertion pipeline on both the main and parallel threads.

🐛 Bug Fix

head_commit.message:
PR #53848: [XLA:GPU] Stripe ragged all-to-all copies across multiple blocks

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53848

## 📝 Summary of Changes

The ragged all-to-all kernel copies data to each peer GPU. Until now the number of CUDA thread blocks depended only on the number of updates, so a large copy with few updates ran on a handful of blocks.

This change picks the number of blocks from the amount of data instead, up to about 128 per launch. The blocks split each update into disjoint stripes and copy them in parallel. It works for any number of updates per peer, and small copies launch the same grid as before.

## 🎯 Justification

In four-way expert parallelism, one update can cover an entire peer's routed activations. Assigning a single block to each peer leaves only four blocks to transfer those activations across four GPUs.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance improvement

## 📊 Benchmark

MaxText on GB200 nodes with four GPUs each: expert parallelism equal to the GPU count, BF16, sequence length 128, batch one per GPU, sparse expert path. The control and patched plugins were built from the same source (XLA `3b0f986389`) and differ only by this change.

| Config           | Model                                | Control (ms) | Patched (ms) | Change |
|------------------|--------------------------------------|-------------:|-------------:|-------:|
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Qwen3-235B-A22B (24 of 94 layers)    |        267.0 |         98.0 |   -63% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Qwen3-30B-A3B                        |        226.5 |        116.2 |   -49% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Gemma4 26B                           |        167.0 |         90.5 |   -46% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Qwen3-480B-A35B (12 of 62 layers)    |        278.5 |        157.5 |   -43% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Mixtral 8x22B (24 of 56 layers)      |        150.0 |         86.5 |   -42% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Mixtral 8x7B †                       |        134.0 |         78.5 |   -41% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | DeepSeek-V2 16B                      |        101.5 |         65.0 |   -36% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | DeepSeek-V2 236B (16 of 60 layers)   |        230.0 |        153.0 |   -33% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B                   |        396.2 |        267.8 |   -32% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | gpt-oss-20B                          |        227.0 |        164.5 |   -28% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (12 of 60 layers)  |        261.5 |        198.0 |   -24% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Llama4 17B-16E (16 of 48 layers)     |        117.0 |         95.0 |   -19% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | gpt-oss-120B †                       |        524.0 |        433.5 |   -17% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Kimi K2 (8 of 61 layers)             |        392.0 |        325.5 |   -17% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | DeepSeek-V4 284B †                   |        852.5 |        720.0 |   -16% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | DeepSeek-V3 671B (16 of 61 layers) † |        890.0 |        759.5 |   -15% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B                      |        221.8 |        207.2 |    -7% |
| 1 node, 4 GPUs   | Llama4 17B-128E (16 of 48 layers) †  |        410.0 |        401.0 |    -2% |
| 2 nodes, 8 GPUs  | Qwen3-30B-A3B                        |        210.9 |        148.1 |   -30% |
| 2 nodes, 8 GPUs  | gpt-oss-120B                         |        587.0 |        503.8 |   -14% |
| 4 nodes, 16 GPUs | Qwen3-30B-A3B                        |        205.2 |        143.2 |   -30% |
| 4 nodes, 16 GPUs | gpt-oss-120B                         |        757.8 |        713.5 |    -6% |

Train step time is the unprofiled median over steps 15–64 of 65-step runs, mean of at least two runs per arm. Rows marked † were measured with the first commit only; the others include the generalization to any number of updates. Qwen3-30B-A3B on one node was measured with both and gave 114.5 ms with the first commit.

- Control and patched losses matched within 0.003 at every step, except for Gemma4 26B, whose loss already differs between two runs of the control plugin.
- In the multi-node runs all GPUs were in one NVLink domain, so every rank was reached directly through the same kernel.
- Two configurations varied between runs with the patched plugin while control stayed steady: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on one node (192–238 ms against 222 ms) and Qwen3-30B-A3B on two nodes (111–182 ms over five runs against 210–213 ms).
- Models listed with a layer count were reduced because their full expert weights do not fit on four GPUs.
- gpt-oss-120B and gpt-oss-20B were measured with the Transformer Engine grouped GEMM disabled; gpt-oss-120B crashes on the first step with it enabled, with or without this change.

## 🧪 Unit Tests

The GPU kernel tests now cover one, two and six updates per peer, the cap on the number of blocks, 8-byte vectors and three peers, and assert the block grid of each case.

## 🧪 Execution Tests

Every benchmarked configuration completed 65 training steps with the patched plugin. These models send one update per peer, so the multi-update path is covered by the kernel tests only.

2ed703615ae2cad29f1fd510b678244dfd7f279b by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Parallelize single-update ragged all-to-all copies

Let multiple CTAs stripe a single large transfer to each peer. Choose the number of blocks from the vectorized input size and cover empty updates and partial stripes in both kernel entry points.

--
8f61a7b39925428f07a4953b56d87becef98ab2e by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Stripe ragged all-to-all copies for any number of updates

The kernel used the z dimension of the block grid both as the number of
updates in a group and as the number of stripes per update, with a special
case for a single update per peer. Derive the number of updates in a group
from the y dimension instead, so that z is only the number of stripes.

Size the stripes from the input for every update count, not just for one
update per peer. The launch dimensions for one update per peer are unchanged.

Cover the block cap, 8-byte vectors, an output count that does not divide
the cap, and groups with more blocks than updates in the kernel tests.

--
e5ebe4e458a5ab7a8f7b8f50b1692fa6a3227988 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix include order in ragged_all_to_all_test.cc

--
98cab09d10d46ee34087c2ead53282df697ab8bd by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Harden the ragged all-to-all kernel tests

Wait for the kernel's stream before reading the outputs back. The readback
of the output-pointer test bypasses the launch stream, and the
symmetric-memory test reads each device through its own stream.

Expose the block grid the kernels are launched with and assert it for every
test case, so that the tests fail if the launch stops using several blocks.

Destroy the NCCL communicators of the symmetric-memory test once their
windows are gone.

--
079d20a5cf429d61afb49b16815a50cd15316ab1 by Shaogang Wang <shawnw@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Synchronize peer streams before the ragged all-to-all test kernel

KernelWithSymmetricMemory zero-fills each output buffer on the stream of its
own device and then launches the kernel on the stream of the first device.
Neither ncclCommInitAll nor ncclCommWindowRegister synchronizes user streams,
so the kernel's writes to a peer device could race with a zero fill still in

head_commit.message:
Add cross-backend CUDA/ROCm dependency checks and consolidate CPU checks

Updates `.github/workflows/bazel_dependency_violations.yml` to run 3 parallel
jobs—one per build configuration:
- `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: consolidates the 3 CPU checks (`gpu`,
  `cuda-only`, `rocm-only`) into separate steps sharing one warm Bazel server,
  saving ~2 cold runner invocations per PR while preserving per-tag step
  reporting and `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` output.
- `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build` (`--config=cuda_clang`)
- `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build` (`--config=rocm_clang_hermetic`)

Extracts the per-tag `bazel cquery` check into
`build_tools/dependencies/check_dependency_violations.sh`, triggers `cquery`
when the workflow or dependency-check scripts themselves change, and bumps the
job timeout from 10 to 15 minutes to accommodate the hermetic ROCm download.

Observed GitHub Actions durations (when build/config files change):
- Before (3 separate CPU jobs): ~3m 20s – 5m 30s each (~11m 50s – 12m 30s total
  runner time; ~5m wall-clock).
- After (3 parallel jobs across CPU, CUDA, and ROCm):
  - `no-gpu-targets-in-cpu-build`: ~3m 30s – 3m 45s (the 2nd and 3rd `cquery`
    steps take only ~1–4s on the warm Bazel server, saving ~8.5 runner-min).
  - `no-rocm-only-targets-in-cuda-build`: ~4m 10s – 6m 05s.
  - `no-cuda-only-targets-in-rocm-build`: ~6m 40s – 7m 10s (~8m headroom under
    the 15-minute timeout).
  - Total: ~14m 30s – 16m 45s runner time (~7m wall-clock) for all 3 configs.

Temporarily keeps lightweight pass-through stub jobs (~5s each on
`ubuntu-latest`) for the legacy `no-cuda-only-targets-in-cpu-build` and
`no-rocm-only-targets-in-cpu-build` check names during the transition; a
follow-up change removes them once CI configs stop waiting on those names.

head_commit.message:
PR #46001: [GPU][Triton][RaggedDot] Autotuner support (PR 7/8)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the 7th in a series of eight aiming to enable the Triton backend for the `ragged-dot` operation using triton group-gemm kernels, based on the experimental tiling strategy.

PR 1/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45995
PR 2/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45996
PR 3/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45997
PR 4/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45998
PR 5/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45999
PR 6/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46000
PR 7/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46001   <---- This PR
PR 8/8: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46002

This PR adds autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions:
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting, Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported() ragged dispatch in the autotuner.
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.

🎯 Justification
The default way for handling ragged-dot ops is to expand the ragged-dot matrix into zero-padded matrices then rewriting the ragged-dot into a batched dot between the padded matrices and the second operand, which results in numerous unnecessary calculations.
Although there are other, more efficient backends (CuDNN and Hipblast), these are not capable of handling all possible configurations.
In this context, having another, more generic Triton backend could enable good performance for ‘ragged-dot’ operations on all targets and for all input configurations.
The order in which backends are selected is as follows:
1. Cudnn if compatible Cuda target or Hipblaslt if compatible HIP target
2. Triton backend if compatible input configuration
3. Default rewriting

5944cf5fa102e1a21157fec89fcbf04f2632c979 by Maxime France-Pillois <mfrancep@amd.com>:

[XTile][RaggedDot] Autotuner support

Add autotuning support for Triton kRaggedDot fusions, which now carry the
generic kTritonFusionKind rather than the legacy kTritonGemmFusionKind.

Autotuner (triton.cc / triton.h):
- GetSupportedConfigsForRaggedDot(): generates a pruned TritonGemmConfig
  search space for all three ragged variants (NonContracting, Contracting,
  Batch).
- ApplyConfig() ragged path: translates a TritonGemmKey into a
  BlockLevelFusionConfig + inner Tile backend config on the kRaggedDot.
- IsSupported(): claim kTritonFusionKind fusions that contain a kRaggedDot,
  before the GEMM-fusion kind check.  Only those: all other generic Triton
  fusions belong to BlockLevelEmitterBackend.  This replaces the previous
  branch, which was unreachable behind the kind check and relied on the
  now-removed xla_gpu_experimental_enable_tiling_propagation debug option.
- BlockLevelEmitterBackend::IsSupported(): skip fusions containing a
  kRaggedDot so that it and TritonBackend cannot both claim them when
  xla_gpu_experimental_all_fusions_with_triton is set.

Pass wiring:
- gpu_profiler.cc: profile ragged-dot fusion timing.
- autotuner_pass.cc: route ragged-dot fusions to the Triton autotuner.
- config_assigner_pass: route ragged-dot Triton fusions to
  ShouldAssignConfigToGemmFusion().  Without this they fall through to
  generic fusion autotuning, which rejects every kCustom fusion, so no
  config would ever be assigned.  They always carry a default
  BlockLevelFusionConfig from GemmRewriter, hence no "already has a
  config" check.
- config_assigner_pass: drop the register-spilling carve-out for
  ragged-dot; kTritonFusionKind is not in the forbidden list, so these
  fusions are already allowed to spill.

Address review feedback on ragged-dot autotuner support

  element type (S8/S16/S32/S64), fill every element of a batched [B, G]
  buffer, and locate it via parameter_number() instead of CHECKing for
  parameter(2).
- triton: in kRaggedBatch mode prune the search space against M rather
  than the batch size.
- config_assigner_pass: forbid autotuning ragged-dot fusions when the
  Triton backend is disabled, instead of failing to find a config.
- Reuse hlo_query::GetFirstInstructionWithOpcode, extract the ragged-dot
  dimension/config/apply helpers, and fix local naming.
- Add unit tests for all of the above.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support CTA cluster synchronization in bitonic sort

Previously, the MLIR bitonic sort emitter only fused compare-and-swap steps
within one CTA's shared-memory tile (`tile_size`), requiring a separate global
kernel launch per step once `xor_mask >= tile_size`.

On Hopper+ GPUs (`sm_90+`), extend tiled bitonic sort across 2-CTA clusters
using distributed shared memory (DSMEM) and cluster barriers, doubling the
in-kernel sort span and cutting global round-trips:
- Add `gpu::BarrierScope` (default `Workgroup`) to `xla_gpu.sync_threads`
  and forward it to `gpu.barrier` in GPU tensor lowering so `GPUToNVVM`
  lowers cluster barriers to `nvvm.cluster.arrive` and `nvvm.cluster.wait`.
- Add a DSMEM pointer-mapping callback hook (`CreateDsmemPointerFn`) in
  `lower_tensors_common` for `"xla_gpu.dsmem"` shared-memory accesses,
  lowering to `nvvm.mapa` (shared -> shared::cluster) inside GPU
  `LowerTensorsPass` so `lower_tensors_common` adds no GPU dialect deps.
- Emit 2-CTA clustered bitonic sort kernels when stages exceed `tile_size`,
  unclustered blocks exceed SM count, and cluster padding is at most 12.5%
  (capping at 2 CTAs avoids GPC fragmentation and register pressure). Cross-CTA
  steps use `gpu.cluster_block_id x` and DSMEM; full tiles keep the unrolled
  fast path while bounds-checked and post-cluster `kIntraTileSort` merges stay
  rolled.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Fast branchless FP8 conversions in XLA intrinsic library.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Add fast branchless FP8 conversions in ExpandFloatOpsPass.

XLA:CPU previously lowered all 8-bit float conversions through the generic `EmitFloatConversion` fallback. On x86-64 AVX2, that fallback emitted over 100 instructions and 700 bytes of stack spills per vector, making fused FP8 kernels roughly 8x slower than `bf16`.

Add portable, branchless scalar and vector MLIR `arith` lowerings in the CPU `ExpandFloatOpsPass` for all eight 8-bit float formats (`f8E4M3FN`, `f8E5M2`, `f8E4M3`, `f8E3M4`, `f8E4M3FNUZ`, `f8E5M2FNUZ`, `f8E4M3B11FNUZ`, and `f8E8M0FNU`). Conversion from 8-bit float supports `f32`, `f64`, `bf16`, and `f16`, using direct upper-bit truncation for `bf16` and a single shift for `f8E5M2` to `f16`. Conversion to 8-bit float supports `f32`, `bf16`, and `f16` with round-to-nearest-even and no double rounding, clamping the subnormal rounding input for fast-math safety.

On an AMD EPYC 7B13 (67.1M elements, single core), `f32` to `f8E4M3FN` and `f32` to `f8E5M2` speed up by 5x, 8-bit float to `f32` speeds up by 1.7x, and fused FP8 elementwise add speeds up by 4x (matching `bf16` memory bandwidth). Verified bit-for-bit across all 2^32 `f32` inputs, all 2^16 `bf16` inputs, and all 2^8 FP8 inputs (including fast-math mode) on x86-64 and ARM64.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1030099919

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Redirect only aliasing uses when copying shared read only values

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Redirect only aliasing uses when copying shared read only values

When `CopyRemover` elides one of several copies of a constant or unaliased
entry parameter, that read only value shares a buffer with other values.
`CopyInsertion::AddSpecialCaseCopies` previously copied the value and replaced
every use. That rewrite turned surviving copies into double copy chains and
routed pure readers through the new copy.

When copying a non root read only array value for buffer sharing, preserve
direct uses that do not forward the value, alias an output in place, produce a
view color output, target `Pin`, or execute in control flow context. After
`DeepCopyInstruction` redirects aliasing uses to the new copy, restore those
preserved operands onto the original instruction. Copies requested by
`custom_buffer_analysis` or root rules still replace every use. Regenerate the
GPU AOT async collective goldens for `SendRecvInWhileLoop`, where a broadcast
fusion now reads constant zero directly.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test`: pins shared constants in while
  loops, read only entry parameters with in place and duplicate operand ops,
  and exclusions for forwarders, control flow calls, `Pin`, views, and custom
  buffer callbacks.
- `//xla/tests/aot_compatibility/gpu:async_collectives_aot_test`: updates v4
  goldens for H100, B200, and GB200.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Fold identity dynamic-update-slice of slice from same source

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fold identity dynamic-update-slice of slice from same source

`AlgebraicSimplifier` did not simplify a `dynamic-update-slice` that writes an
unmodified `slice` or `dynamic-slice` of its base operand back to the same
indices. Such updates act as noops but survive into buffer assignment and force
unnecessary copies and fusions.

Fold `dynamic-update-slice(x, slice(x, starts, limits, 1), starts)` and
`dynamic-update-slice(x, dynamic-slice(x, starts, sizes), starts)` directly to
`x` in `HandleDynamicUpdateSlice`. Both `dynamic-slice` and
`dynamic-update-slice` clamp each scalar start index to the same range, so
matching symbolic or clamped constant offsets fold with exact equality. Bail
out on dynamic, empty, buffer, or mixed precision shapes, vector indices, and
incompatible layouts, shardings, or control predecessors. Existing program
outputs are unchanged.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pins unstrided
  `slice` and `dynamic-slice` identity folds and rejects strided, shifted,
  swapped, dynamic, and resharding updates.

[XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

config are never hoisted.

  hoisting and rejects same layout, alternate memory, host compute, and backend

name: CI
display_title: Serialize per-device OOM retries in CommonPjRtClient.

head_commit.message:
Serialize per-device OOM retries in CommonPjRtClient.

When multiple threads hit `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` concurrently on the same device
during execution preparation, each thread independently triggers OOM recovery
(such as program eviction and memory defragmentation) and retries at the same
time. This causes redundant double-OOM recoveries and memory thrashing.

* Add per-addressable-device `DeviceOomState` and `OomSequencer` in
  `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.h` and `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client.cc`.
* Add `CommonPjRtClient::RunWithOomRetries`, which runs lock-free when the
  device is not under OOM, serializes recovery and retry attempts per device on
  `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, and skips redundant recovery when another thread has
  already bumped the device OOM generation.
* Route `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::ExecutePrepareWithOomRetries` through
  `RunWithOomRetries`, resetting `launch_args` before waiting or recovering so
  partial buffer holds are released first.
* Add unit tests for `OomSequencer` concurrency, serialization, generation
  skipping, termination, and per-device independence in
  `xla/pjrt/common_pjrt_client_test.cc`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add embeddable CUB single-tile radix sort kernels

Currently XLA executes CUDA CUB sorts via FFI custom calls to `cub::DeviceRadixSort` and `cub::DeviceSegmentedRadixSort`, which ties the GPU runtime to CUB host APIs and prevents embedding sort kernels in AOT artifacts.

So this change adds the sharded `embeddable_cuda_library(..., register_with_cudart = False)` kernel infrastructure under `xla/backends/gpu/libraries/cub/` together with the unified single-tile radix sort kernels (covering both unbatched and batched segments that fit in a single thread block) across all 12 keys-only and 18 key-value pair types. Each device `XlaChainedPolicy` is built from `cub_sort_policy.h` and checked with `static_assert`s so host planning and compiled single-architecture CUBINs stay in lockstep across CCCL versions.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Create reduce-scatter through elementwise ops between all-reduce and dynamic-slice

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Do not look through fusions or computation roots when matching elementwise ops for reduce-scatter

Address review comments on the elementwise chain between an all-reduce and
its dynamic-slice:

- Check the opcode with HloInstruction::IsOpElementwise instead of
  IsElementwise(), which also holds for elementwise fusions. A fusion cannot
  be re-created with a different shape, as its fused computation keeps the
  original shapes.
- Do not match a chain if the all-reduce or one of the chain instructions is
  the root of its computation. A root stays live after its only user is
  replaced, so it could not be removed.
- Derive the shapes of the re-created instructions from the original shapes
  instead of building new ones, so that their layout is kept.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

With default flags, porting a `uint8` image pipeline to JAX on CPU gives
results that differ from NumPy and XLA:GPU as soon as the inputs are large
enough to be fused into a `__ynn_fusion`. For example:

```python
f = jax.jit(lambda a, b: jnp.max(a, axis=0, keepdims=True) + b)
f(np.full((1024, 17), 255, np.uint8), np.full((1024, 17), 103, np.uint8))
```

returns `255` instead of `102`, and in a `uint8` contrast stretch 50-89% of
the pixels on 480x640 frames are wrong. `s8` `127 + 1` gives `127` instead of
`-128`, and `s8` `7 / 2` gives `4` instead of `3`. XLA:GPU, NumPy,
`HloEvaluator`, constant folding and XLA:CPU on small (unfused) inputs all
wrap and truncate.

Reported by @SomyaPadhy4501 in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51826
(found while porting an image pipeline, and also by a CPU-vs-GPU integer
fuzzer).

Root cause: `IsElementwiseOpSupportedByYnn` accepts `S8`/`U8` for every op in
`GetYnnBinaryOpMap()` and `GetYnnUnaryOpMap()`. YNNPACK's 8-bit add, subtract,
multiply and power saturate and its integer divide rounds. It has no 8-bit
unary kernels, so it computes them in fp32 and saturates the result (`u8`
`negate(1)` gives `0`, `s8` `negate(-128)` and `abs(-128)` give `127`). Any of
these ops fused next to a YNN reduction (the default `REDUCE` fusion type)
changes the result.

Fix: for `S8`/`U8` binary ops, only offload `maximum` and `minimum`, and for
`S8`/`U8` unary ops, only offload `convert` and `sign`. These give the same
results either way. Other 8-bit elementwise ops fall back to the regular
XLA:CPU emitter. Floating-point ops, integer reductions and converts are
unchanged. This follows the earlier fixes that stop offloading ops
YNNPACK cannot compute exactly (#48378, #49899).

Tested: new `YnnReduceInt8EltwiseTest.EltwiseAfterReduceWraps` in
`//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test` runs the issue's pattern
(max/min reduce + broadcast + add/subtract/multiply/divide/power on `u8`/`s8`
`[1024,17]`), and new `YnnReduceInt8UnaryTest.UnaryBeforeReduceWraps` runs
`negate`/`abs` feeding a max reduce. All 9 cases fail before this change (255
vs 102, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127 vs -56, 4 vs 3, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127
vs -128, 127 vs -128) and pass after it. Both tests also check with
`MatchOptimizedHlo` that only the reduce stays in `__ynn_fusion`.
`YnnReduceTest.Int8MaximumAfterReduceIsFused` checks that `s8` maximum is
still fused into `__ynn_fusion`.

name: CI
display_title: Validate dimensions before narrowing in SelectKExecuteFfiHandler.

head_commit.message:
Validate dimensions before narrowing in SelectKExecuteFfiHandler.

`SelectKExecuteFfiHandler` previously cast `int64_t` input and output dimensions directly to `uint32_t` without bounds checks. Malformed `__gpu$TopK` shapes could trigger divide-by-zero in RAFT `warpsort::calc_launch_parameter` when `batch` or `n` is zero. Oversized shapes could silently truncate on cast or wrap 32-bit `batch * k`, causing out-of-bounds GPU writes in `segmented_sort_by_key`.

Validate `batch`, `n`, and `k` in `int64_t` before narrowing to `uint32_t`, matching the invariants in `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytesImpl`. Reject non-positive dimensions, `k > n`, `batch` or `n` exceeding `INT32_MAX`, and `batch * k` exceeding `UINT32_MAX` with `InvalidArgumentError`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Fast branchless FP8 conversions in XLA intrinsic library.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Fast branchless FP8 conversions in XLA intrinsic library.

XLA:CPU previously expanded scalar FP8 `truncf`/`extf` inline through the generic `EmitFloatConversion` fallback in `emitters::ExpandFloatOpsPass` before `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` could run. On x86-64 AVX2, that prevented vector intrinsic lowering via `VecDesc` and emitted heavy scalar/spilled code. Even the existing `xla.fptrunc` path (`EmitFxxToF8E`) relied on `EmitReducePrecisionIR` plus halfway-point fixups and lacked an `fpext` intrinsic, `F8E8M0FNU`, `BF16` sources, and 16-lane vector variants.

This change consolidates CPU FP8 conversions into `xla/codegen/intrinsic/`:

- Replace `EmitFxxToF8E` in `FpTrunc` (`fptrunc.{h,cc}`) with a branchless RTNE implementation for `{F16, BF16, F32, F64}` -> all 8 FP8 formats (`F8E4M3FN`, `F8E5M2`, `F8E4M3`, `F8E3M4`, `F8E4M3FNUZ`, `F8E5M2FNUZ`, `F8E4M3B11FNUZ`, `F8E8M0FNU`), scalar and `{2, 4, 8, 16}`-lane vectors, using a fast-math-safe `umin` clamp and magic-add subnormal rounding.
- Add an `FpExt` intrinsic (`fpext.{h,cc}`) for all 8 FP8 formats -> `{F16, BF16, F32, F64}` (scalar and `{2, 4, 8, 16}`-lane vectors), including a single-shift `F8E5M2 -> F16` path and upper-16-bit shift for `BF16`.
- Fix `IntrinsicFunctionLib::Vectorizations()` to enforce `prefer_vector_width` against `max(BitWidth(arg), BitWidth(ret))` so narrow-to-wide `FpExt` ops do not exceed the target vector width (e.g. capping `f8 -> f32` at `v8` on AVX2).
- Add an `expand_f8_conversions` option (default `true`, keeping GPU unchanged) on `emitters::ExpandFloatOpsPass`, set to `false` on CPU in `FusionCompiler` so scalar FP8 `truncf`/`extf` and min/max lower through `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` and vectorize via `VecDesc`.
- Add exhaustive in-tree tests in `fptrunc_test.cc` and `fpext_test.cc`, vector width-cap tests in `intrinsic_lib_test.cc`, MLIR lit tests, an end-to-end `CpuFusionEmitterTest`, and FP8 conversion benchmarks in `elementwise_benchmark_test.cc`.

Single-core AMD EPYC 7B13 (AVX2) median times from `elementwise_benchmark_test` with `--xla_disable_hlo_passes=cpu-parallel-task-assigner` (3–5 reps):

| Benchmark | Size | HEAD (`EmitFloatConversion`) | Existing `xla.fptrunc` | New `xla.fptrunc`/`fpext` | Speedup (vs HEAD / existing) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `F32 -> BF16` (ref) | 524K / 16.8M | 77.2 us / 5.38 ms | 77.2 us / 5.38 ms | 79.3 us / 5.18 ms | — |
| `F32 -> F8E4M3FN` | 524K / 16.8M | 777.6 us / 24.58 ms | 377.9 us / 12.04 ms | 142.5 us / 5.03 ms | 5.5x / 2.7x (4.9x / 2.4x) |
| `F32 -> F8E5M2` | 524K / 16.8M | 790.1 us / 25.23 ms | 463.2 us / 14.14 ms | 156.6 us / 5.32 ms | 5.0x / 3.0x (4.7x / 2.7x) |
| `F8E4M3FN -> F32` | 524K / 16.8M | 260.9 us / 8.21 ms | — | 145.6 us / 4.82 ms | 1.8x (1.7x) |
| `F8E5M2 -> F32` | 524K / 16.8M | 282.5 us / 8.90 ms | — | 177.9 us / 5.82 ms | 1.6x (1.5x) |

Tested: `fptrunc_test`, `fpext_test`, `intrinsic_lib_test`, `emitters/transforms/...`, `backends/cpu/codegen/...`, and `convert_test_cpu` in `-c opt`, `-c fastbuild`, and `--cpu=arm -c opt`.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Fast branchless FP8 conversions in XLA intrinsic library.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Fast branchless FP8 conversions in XLA intrinsic library.

XLA:CPU previously expanded scalar FP8 `truncf`/`extf` inline through the generic `EmitFloatConversion` fallback in `emitters::ExpandFloatOpsPass` before `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` could run. On x86-64 AVX2, that prevented vector intrinsic lowering via `VecDesc` and emitted heavy scalar/spilled code. Even the existing `xla.fptrunc` path (`EmitFxxToF8E`) relied on `EmitReducePrecisionIR` plus halfway-point fixups and lacked an `fpext` intrinsic, `F8E8M0FNU`, `BF16` sources, and 16-lane vector variants.

This change consolidates CPU FP8 conversions into `xla/codegen/intrinsic/`:

- Replace `EmitFxxToF8E` in `FpTrunc` (`fptrunc.{h,cc}`) with a branchless RTNE implementation for `{F16, BF16, F32, F64}` -> all 8 FP8 formats (`F8E4M3FN`, `F8E5M2`, `F8E4M3`, `F8E3M4`, `F8E4M3FNUZ`, `F8E5M2FNUZ`, `F8E4M3B11FNUZ`, `F8E8M0FNU`), scalar and `{2, 4, 8, 16}`-lane vectors, using a fast-math-safe `umin` clamp and magic-add subnormal rounding.
- Add an `FpExt` intrinsic (`fpext.{h,cc}`) for all 8 FP8 formats -> `{F16, BF16, F32, F64}` (scalar and `{2, 4, 8, 16}`-lane vectors), including a single-shift `F8E5M2 -> F16` path and upper-16-bit shift for `BF16`.
- Fix `IntrinsicFunctionLib::Vectorizations()` to enforce `prefer_vector_width` against `max(BitWidth(arg), BitWidth(ret))` so narrow-to-wide `FpExt` ops do not exceed the target vector width (e.g. capping `f8 -> f32` at `v8` on AVX2).
- Add an `expand_f8_conversions` option (default `true`, keeping GPU unchanged) on `emitters::ExpandFloatOpsPass`, set to `false` on CPU in `FusionCompiler` so scalar FP8 `truncf`/`extf` and min/max lower through `LowerXlaIntrinsicLibPass` and vectorize via `VecDesc`.
- Add exhaustive in-tree tests in `fptrunc_test.cc` and `fpext_test.cc`, vector width-cap tests in `intrinsic_lib_test.cc`, MLIR lit tests, an end-to-end `CpuFusionEmitterTest`, and FP8 conversion benchmarks in `elementwise_benchmark_test.cc`.

Single-core AMD EPYC 7B13 (AVX2) median times from `elementwise_benchmark_test` with `--xla_disable_hlo_passes=cpu-parallel-task-assigner` (3–5 reps):

| Benchmark | Size | HEAD (`EmitFloatConversion`) | Existing `xla.fptrunc` | New `xla.fptrunc`/`fpext` | Speedup (vs HEAD / existing) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `F32 -> BF16` (ref) | 524K / 16.8M | 77.2 us / 5.38 ms | 77.2 us / 5.38 ms | 79.3 us / 5.18 ms | — |
| `F32 -> F8E4M3FN` | 524K / 16.8M | 777.6 us / 24.58 ms | 377.9 us / 12.04 ms | 142.5 us / 5.03 ms | 5.5x / 2.7x (4.9x / 2.4x) |
| `F32 -> F8E5M2` | 524K / 16.8M | 790.1 us / 25.23 ms | 463.2 us / 14.14 ms | 156.6 us / 5.32 ms | 5.0x / 3.0x (4.7x / 2.7x) |
| `F8E4M3FN -> F32` | 524K / 16.8M | 260.9 us / 8.21 ms | — | 145.6 us / 4.82 ms | 1.8x (1.7x) |
| `F8E5M2 -> F32` | 524K / 16.8M | 282.5 us / 8.90 ms | — | 177.9 us / 5.82 ms | 1.6x (1.5x) |

Tested: `fptrunc_test`, `fpext_test`, `intrinsic_lib_test`, `emitters/transforms/...`, `backends/cpu/codegen/...`, and `convert_test_cpu` in `-c opt`, `-c fastbuild`, and `--cpu=arm -c opt`.

head_commit.message:
Expand RAFT select_k GPU runtime tests across shapes and dtypes.

`select_k_exec_raft_test.cc` previously ran only one WarpSort shape (`4x4096`, `k=32`) with a hardcoded 32 MiB scratch buffer, small `uint64_t` keys, and `float`-only command-buffer execution, leaving Radix paths, GPU scratch sizing, unsigned sign-bit ordering, and non-`float` FFI dispatch untested on GPU.

Parameterize `RaftSelectKShapeTest` across 7 shapes covering WarpSort (`kWarpImmediate`, `kWarpFiltered`, `kWarpDistributedShm`, `k == n`) and Radix (`kRadix11bits`, `kRadix8bits`, `kRadix11bitsExtraPass`) with scratch sized by `EstimateRaftSelectKScratchBytes*`. Shift `uint64_t` inputs across the sign bit while including the minimum non-zero key `1`, and template `RunCommandBufferTest` across `float`, `bfloat16`, and `uint64_t`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

With default flags, porting a `uint8` image pipeline to JAX on CPU gives
results that differ from NumPy and XLA:GPU as soon as the inputs are large
enough to be fused into a `__ynn_fusion`. For example:

```python
f = jax.jit(lambda a, b: jnp.max(a, axis=0, keepdims=True) + b)
f(np.full((1024, 17), 255, np.uint8), np.full((1024, 17), 103, np.uint8))
```

returns `255` instead of `102`, and in a `uint8` contrast stretch 50-89% of
the pixels on 480x640 frames are wrong. `s8` `127 + 1` gives `127` instead of
`-128`, and `s8` `7 / 2` gives `4` instead of `3`. XLA:GPU, NumPy,
`HloEvaluator`, constant folding and XLA:CPU on small (unfused) inputs all
wrap and truncate.

Reported by @SomyaPadhy4501 in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51826
(found while porting an image pipeline, and also by a CPU-vs-GPU integer
fuzzer).

Root cause: `IsElementwiseOpSupportedByYnn` accepts `S8`/`U8` for every op in
`GetYnnBinaryOpMap()` and `GetYnnUnaryOpMap()`. YNNPACK's 8-bit add, subtract,
multiply and power saturate and its integer divide rounds. It has no 8-bit
unary kernels, so it computes them in fp32 and saturates the result (`u8`
`negate(1)` gives `0`, `s8` `negate(-128)` and `abs(-128)` give `127`). Any of
these ops fused next to a YNN reduction (the default `REDUCE` fusion type)
changes the result.

Fix: for `S8`/`U8` binary ops, only offload `maximum` and `minimum`, and for
`S8`/`U8` unary ops, only offload `convert` and `sign`. These give the same
results either way. Other 8-bit elementwise ops fall back to the regular
XLA:CPU emitter. Floating-point ops, integer reductions and converts are
unchanged. This follows the earlier fixes that stop offloading ops
YNNPACK cannot compute exactly (#48378, #49899).

Tested: new `YnnReduceInt8EltwiseTest.EltwiseAfterReduceWraps` in
`//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test` runs the issue's pattern
(max/min reduce + broadcast + add/subtract/multiply/divide/power on `u8`/`s8`
`[1024,17]`), and new `YnnReduceInt8UnaryTest.UnaryBeforeReduceWraps` runs
`negate`/`abs` feeding a max reduce. All 9 cases fail before this change (255
vs 102, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127 vs -56, 4 vs 3, 127 vs -128, 0 vs 255, 127
vs -128, 127 vs -128) and pass after it. Both tests also check with
`MatchOptimizedHlo` that only the reduce stays in `__ynn_fusion`.
`YnnReduceTest.Int8MaximumAfterReduceIsFused` checks that `s8` maximum is
still fused into `__ynn_fusion`.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support sign in the block-level Triton emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support sign in the block-level Triton emitter.

Fusions containing `sign` (`HloOpcode::kSign`) previously fell back to the native emitters because `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` excluded `kSign` and `EmitElementwise` did not handle it.

Enable `HloOpcode::kSign` for signed integral types (`s8`, `s16`, `s32`, `s64`) and floating-point types (`f16`, `bf16`, `f32`, `f64`), emit and allow `stablehlo.sign` in XTile, and lower `stablehlo.sign` in `StablehloLowerToArithPass` to four pure `arith` comparisons and selects. Lowering via `math.copysign` was rejected because Triton's `ConvertTritonToTritonGPU` pass does not legalize `math.copysign`. Using `cmpf olt`/`ogt` with `arith.select` preserves the sign bit of `-0.0` and `NaN` values identically to `HloEvaluator`, and using `cmpi slt`/`sgt` with `arith.select` handles `INT_MIN` without overflow. Unsupported types (complex, FP8/FP4, sub-byte integers) remain unlowered so support checks stay in sync with codegen.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support is-finite in the block-level Triton emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support is-finite in the block-level Triton emitter.

Fusions containing `is-finite` previously fell back to the native emitters because `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` excluded `HloOpcode::kIsFinite` and Triton's `ConvertTritonToTritonGPU` pass does not legalize `math.isfinite`.

Add `HloOpcode::kIsFinite` for `f16`, `bf16`, `f32`, and `f64` in `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` and lower `math.isfinite` in `UnsupportedElementwiseToTritonPass` to `arith.cmpf one, math.absf(x), +inf`. Lowering in the Triton-specific pass preserves `math.isfinite` in the shared XTile emitter used by the CPU backend, avoids `third_party/triton` patches, and avoids libdevice call overhead and missing 16-bit libdevice helpers while matching the native MLIR emitter's IEEE-754 semantics (`±inf` and `±NaN` return `false`; finite values including `±0` and subnormals return `true`).
