name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Initialize dynamic dimension sizes in MakeFakeLiteral and validate them in PJRT linearization

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Initialize dynamic dimension sizes in MakeFakeLiteral and validate them in PJRT linearization

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Follow-up to PR #47804  for issue #47379.

`MakeFakeLiteral` constructs dynamic-shaped literals without ever setting
their dynamic-dimension sizes, and literal construction leaves those metadata
slots uninitialized - so every fake argument generated for a dynamic-shaped
parameter (e.g. by `run_hlo_module`) carries an uninitialized-memory "runtime
size" (values like -1969319720 observed). Depending on what the garbage
happens to be, the same module then runs, produces nonsense, or crashes: at
current HEAD the module from #47379 segfaults on GPU during the host-to-device
transfer because the garbage size drives the linearization transpose out of
bounds, and the Interpreter silently carries the garbage size.
Two changes:
- `MakeFakeLiteral` now initializes every dynamic dimension's size to its
  bound (in both the random and the non-random paths), so generated literals
  are always well-formed.
- `CommonPjRtClient::Linearize` now rejects a dynamic size above its
  dimension bound with `InvalidArgument` before writing anything. The sizes
  arrive as `uint32`, so negative garbage from corrupted literals is caught
  by the same comparison. This turns what was an unchecked out-of-bounds
  write into a clean error on every platform that uses the common
  linearization path.
With this change alone, the module from #47379 runs cleanly on the
Interpreter and on GPU with a well-formed input (the remaining CPU crash is
the separate transfer defect fixed by #47804; with both changes, CPU, GPU,
and Interpreter all agree on the output).

## 🎯 Justification

Fuzzed and test-generated modules with bounded-dynamic parameters currently
exercise undefined behavior on every platform, which makes crash reports
against dynamic shapes hard to trust (platform-dependent, run-dependent). A
generated argument must be in-contract, and the transfer layer must not turn
a corrupted size into memory corruption.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

- 🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`LiteralUtilTest.MakeFakeLiteralInitializesDynamicSizes`: a `f32[2,<=10]`
fake literal reports dynamic size 10 through both the seeded and the

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Keep batch sharding for grouped convolutions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Keep batch sharding for grouped convolutions

## 📝 Summary of Changes

Fixes #47945.

The SPMD partitioner currently gives up on any convolution with
`feature_group_count > 1` that is not depthwise shaped
(`kernel_input_feature_dim > 1`): `PartitionConv` returns an engaged null
optional, which aborts the whole `PartitionDot` strategy search, so the
partitioner falls back to replicating the operands. For a conv that is only
sharded on the batch dimension this means: all-gather the full batch on
every partition, run the full-batch grouped conv redundantly everywhere,
then dynamic-slice the local shard back out. The same conv with
`feature_group_count = 1` partitions into a local conv with no collectives.
The grouping only constrains the feature dimensions, so when none of the
group-relevant feature dimensions is partitioned (input feature, kernel
input feature, kernel output feature, output feature), the grouping is
transparent to the generic dot partitioning. This change makes
`PartitionConv` fall through (`std::nullopt`) to the generic logic in
exactly that case, so a batch-sharded grouped conv partitions like its
dense counterpart: each partition runs the grouped conv on its local batch
shard against the replicated kernel. `CreateShardedConvolution` recomputes
`feature_group_count` from the sharded operand shapes, and with feature
dims unpartitioned that reproduces the original group count, so the local
conv is correct as-is.
When any of the four feature dimensions is partitioned the behavior is
unchanged (hard bail, replicate fallback): the generic dot logic must not
see those cases, because contracting-dim or output-feature partitioning
would recompute wrong groups on feature shards.

## 🎯 Justification

The reporter measured a production 8xB200 data-parallel training job where
the redundant grouped-conv all-gathers account for ~30% of device time and
the full-batch grouped convs ~45%. Per-partition compute and memory scale
with the global batch (N times the local batch on N partitions). The
repro in the issue shows the exact all-gather + full conv + dynamic-slice
pattern on 8 forced CPU devices, so it is backend-independent.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`PartitionConvWithFeatureGroupCountBatchSharded` in
`spmd_partitioner_test.cc`: partitions a `feature_group_count=2`,
`kernel_input_feature=16` conv sharded `[8,1,1,1]` on batch for 8 devices,
and asserts the root is a local `f32[16,32,32,32]` convolution of the two
parameters with `feature_group_count=2` and that the module contains no
all-gather and no dynamic-slice. The test fails before this change (root is
a dynamic-slice of a replicated full-batch conv behind an all-gather) and
passes with it. All existing tests in `//xla/service/spmd/...` pass; the
existing grouped-conv tests (all depthwise-shaped or feature-sharded) are
unaffected.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

The issue's JAX reproducer on 8 forced CPU devices: with this change the
grouped case compiles to a local conv with zero all-gathers, matching the
`feature_group_count=1` control.

display_title: [PJRT] Restore --xla_dump_hlo_snapshots for single-device GPU executions

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Restore --xla_dump_hlo_snapshots for single-device GPU executions

## 📝 Summary of Changes
`CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute` now dumps the optimized-module `HloSnapshot` (module plus argument and result literals) for single-device executions on clients that take the general execution path, i.e. the StreamExecutor GPU client. It reuses the `MaybeDumpHloSnapshot` helper that the CPU fast path in the same function already uses, dumping once before the run (crash-safe, without results) and once after with the results, to the same `*.snapshot.<run_id>.pb` file name. Executables that do not expose an `HloModule` (`GetHloModule()` not implemented) are skipped, so nothing changes for them.

## 🎯 Justification

Fixes #39194.

GPU snapshot dumping silently stopped working when GPU execution moved from `LocalExecutable::RunAsync` (which dumped snapshots) to calling `GpuExecutable::ExecuteThunks` directly, between jax[cuda12] 0.5.0 and 0.5.3 as bisected in the issue. The CPU client reimplemented snapshot dumping at the PjRt layer, and that code has since moved into the CPU-only fast path of `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute`, but the general path never got the equivalent, which akuegel confirmed in the issue. This restores the lost behavior next to the CPU implementation, with the same gates and file format.
`--xla_dump_hlo_unoptimized_snapshots` was unaffected and stays unchanged.
Scope notes, matching the CPU path: snapshots are dumped for single-device executions only; if inputs were donated, the post-run argument read fails gracefully and the pre-run snapshot is kept. With the flag off the added cost per execution is one `GetHloModule()` call (a `shared_ptr` copy on the StreamExecutor executable) and two flag checks.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

## 🧪 Unit Tests:

`StreamExecutorGpuClientTest.HloSnapshot` in `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test.cc`, a port of `PjRtCpuClientTest.HloSnapshot`: compiles an add module with the flag set, executes, and verifies the dumped snapshot's argument and result literals. Fails before this change (no snapshot files are produced), passes with it. The CPU tests `PjRtCpuClientTest.HloSnapshot*` are unchanged and still pass.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:

`bazel test //xla/pjrt/gpu:se_gpu_pjrt_client_test` on a single GPU. Requires 1 GPU.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Test YNNPACK fusion exp near FLT_MIN/DBL_MIN under FTZ.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Test YNNPACK fusion exp near FLT_MIN/DBL_MIN under FTZ.

`YnnUnaryOpTest` tests `exponential` with nonzero absolute tolerances (`2e-38` for `f32`, `2e-308` for `f64`), which mask large relative errors in the lowest normal binades when flush-to-zero (FTZ) is enabled. On CPUs without hardware FMA (or with YNNPACK FMA/AVX-512 kernels disabled), YNNPACK's non-FMA `exp` previously rounded a subnormal `2^b * expm1(r)` intermediate that flushed to zero, causing up to 41% relative error on normal outputs.

Add `YnnExpFlushToZeroTest.ExpNearSmallestNormal` to check `f32` and `f64` `__ynn_fusion` `exponential` across `[ln(min) + 0.01, ln(min) + 2.01]` with zero absolute tolerance (`aabs = 0`) and 4-ULP relative tolerance.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support is-finite in the block-level Triton emitter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support is-finite in the block-level Triton emitter.

Fusions containing `is-finite` previously fell back to the native emitters because `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` excluded `HloOpcode::kIsFinite` and Triton's `ConvertTritonToTritonGPU` pass does not legalize `math.isfinite`.

Add `HloOpcode::kIsFinite` for `f16`, `bf16`, `f32`, and `f64` in `TritonSupportedUnaryElementwiseOps` and lower `math.isfinite` in `UnsupportedElementwiseToTritonPass` to `arith.cmpf one, math.absf(x), +inf`. Lowering in the Triton-specific pass preserves `math.isfinite` in the shared XTile emitter used by the CPU backend, avoids `third_party/triton` patches, and avoids libdevice call overhead and missing 16-bit libdevice helpers while matching the native MLIR emitter's IEEE-754 semantics (`±inf` and `±NaN` return `false`; finite values including `±0` and subnormals return `true`).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1030664470

display_title: [PJRT] Restore --xla_dump_hlo_snapshots for single-device GPU executions

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Restore --xla_dump_hlo_snapshots for single-device GPU executions

Optimized-module HLO snapshot dumping was lost on GPU when execution moved
off LocalExecutable::RunAsync onto the direct GpuExecutable::ExecuteThunks
path. The CPU client kept its own dump, which now lives in the CPU-only
fast path of CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::Execute; clients that take the
general path (StreamExecutor GPU among them) never dump.

Dump the snapshot in the general single-device path as well: once before
the run (crash-safe, without results) and once after with the result
literals, using the same MaybeDumpHloSnapshot helper and file name as the
CPU path. Executables that do not expose an HloModule are skipped.

Adds a GPU regression test mirroring PjRtCpuClientTest.HloSnapshot.

Fixes #39194.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add CUDA CUB sort thunk emitter

To replace the runtime CUB FFI custom-call handlers with AOT-embeddable thunks, the compiler needs to turn a `CubSortExecutionPlan` and the embedded CUBIN kernel specs into an executable `ThunkSequence`.

So this change adds `cub_sort_thunk_emitter` and `cub_sort_thunk_emitter_registration` as `cuda-only` targets using the native custom-call thunk-folding infrastructure (`NativeCustomCallHandlerRegistry`), avoiding any `if_cuda_is_configured` branching or non-CUDA stubs. The emitter computes Onesweep histogram occupancy statically from `DeviceDescription` and CUBIN ELF attributes via `cuda_occupancy.h`, packs kernel arguments via `KernelArgsPackingSpec`, and emits a flat `ThunkSequence` of `CustomKernelThunk`s with strict pure-Read/pure-Write `BufferUse` slices for `CommandBufferThunk` capture and update.
